items.title: Emmanuel Sayles Interview, 1961-01-29
items.q: Binge got the idea of taking the show and, and building this band with, uh, with Lee Collins and David Jones as the leader of it, see. This, this Binge fellow, he's the guy? Sam Binge, that, you know, that, where we played at Fowler, that place, on Royal Street, yeah, yeah. So, um, we worked there.

ctx.x: You missed out the, uh, the Lee Collins period there. Well, I, well, that, oh, yeah, that's right,

that's right. That was, that was before Sidney Desmond, I mean Sidney Desmond, because there was, there was a fella named John Morell, banjo player. He had a job at the La Vida, as a jitney dance. That's right. And, um, and that band was, the leader was John Morell, the banjo player, and, uh, Lee Collins on trumpet. Thereto Poinnell on alto and David Jones on tenor. Yeah. Uh, Joe Rovershaw on piano, uh, and, uh, Albert Martin, I think, the drummer. Oh, Albert Martin. Yeah. On drum, and I took John Morell's play.…

items.title: Emmanuel Sayles Interview, 1979-12-05
items.q: We had trumpet, sax, double uncrowned it, and David Jones on tenor.

ctx.x: How long did you stay in Pensacola?

Oh, I think it was, let's see, I went there in 24, I must have came around about, no, about 20 years, about three years, about 27 years. I said, well, when the job was closed and we left Pensacola, and one stayed in Mobile, and they had a union there. They had a union in Jacksonville. We didn't have no union, black union in New Orleans. And when I was coming back, I told my daddy, this thing was really getting bad. items.title: Emmanuel Sayles Interview, 1959-01-17
items.q: So we, that band, built up to be a pretty good band on the Pelican, because we would rehearse and we would get good arrangement down through the direction of David John.

ctx.x: Did you ever hear Alonzo Ross? Alonzo Ross. Alonzo Ross, he was a piano player I think over there. From where? Around Jacksonville, I think.

Well, I probably met him, a lot of the guys. He went to New York. Yeah. Well, that happened years later because now I want to get, you still get on that same kick in Jacksonville. Now, Eagle Eyes had came out somewhere and heard our band. In fact, we even went up and sat in with the band. And he liked me, who I played bands, he liked the way Alvin Morgan played the bass, and he liked the way Edmund Hall played his playing and sax. And he wanted us to quit the band. That we had always promised that we would come…
Oh, excuse me. Did you say who the piano player was originally? Emma Barron.
